author: macro-strategist-cyrus-daruwalla
description: Does an EQUAL-WEIGHT ensemble of the 4 new gauges (CAPE-India, US term spread, US credit spread, Buffett-indicator) -- with and without breadth-thrust -- beat the existing valuation-band (market_state.EY_hist_zscore_expanding, the current M-term baseline) on forward-return prediction, crash-risk prediction, and drop-one/era-split robustness? All gauges oriented so positive = cheap/bullish before averaging (na-aware mean).
data: ALPHA_RANKER/rnd/wave4/w4mac_support/w4mac_gauges_panel.parquet (this session's build); components = W4MAC_cape_india, W4MAC_yield_curve (US term spread leg only), W4MAC_credit_spread, W4MAC_buffett_indicator, W4MAC_breadth_thrust cards.
interpretation: [OPINION] Three honest findings, none of them a clean 'ensemble wins': (1) On RAW predictive magnitude, single gauges beat every ensemble on both axes -- g_valband_EY is the best return-predictor (0.26/0.277) and g_buffett is the best crash-risk-predictor (0.489), and averaging either into a 4-7-gauge blend DILUTES it (ensemble maxdd tops out at 0.328, well below Buffett-alone's 0.489). Unweighted averaging with genuinely weak/unstable legs (CAPE, US term spread, India-10y-change) drags down the strong legs. (2) On DROP-ONE-BEAR robustness, the picture flips: g_valband_EY's positive return-correlation is NOT dropone-stable (sign nearly zeroes out and briefly flips negative without GFC in the sample) -- its edge is more concentrated in one historical crisis than it looks from the full-sample number alone. The 4-and-5-gauge ensembles (excluding the noisier 7-gauge/all-in version) ARE dropone-stable, and with an unusually TIGHT range across which bear is dropped (0.057-0.075 for the 4-gauge blend) -- i.e. their sign and rough magnitude do not depend on any single crisis the way the single best gauges do. (3) On ERA-SPLIT, nothing tested here is clean except g_valband_EY and g_breadth_thrust (both individually) -- every multi-gauge ensemble variant fails a simple pre/post-2015-16 split, largely because term-spread and Buffett-proxy each individually flip sign around 2016-2020 for different, unrelated regime reasons (Fed policy regime vs India market re-rating), and averaging does not cancel that instability, it just dilutes the magnitude while carrying the instability through.
overall_verdict: The ensemble does NOT beat valuation-band-alone (or Buffett-alone) on raw predictive power on EITHER axis tested. Its actual advantage is narrower than 'more robust overall': it is more robust specifically to WHICH SINGLE HISTORICAL CRISIS gets dropped (the property ABSOLUTE_SCORER_SPEC §4.2 explicitly gates on) than the valuation-band is by itself -- at the cost of a materially weaker standalone signal on both return-prediction and crash-risk. Given M's own design intent (a THIN, sign-only, slow-moving regime layer, not a fitted return model -- ABSOLUTE_SCORER_SPEC §0/§3), that trade (less magnitude, less single-crisis dependency) is arguably the right one for M's stated purpose, but it is a genuine trade, not a free robustness win. Recommendation: keep valuation-band (EY) as M's primary input per the existing spec; ADD Buffett-indicator as a SEPARATE, explicitly-labeled crash-risk conditioner (its 0.489 maxdd correlation is too strong to bury inside an unweighted average) rather than folding all 4-5 new gauges into one blended M term.
confidence: MEDIUM on the 'ensemble does not raw-beat single-best-gauges' finding (clean, consistent across both target axes and all 3 ensemble variants tried). MEDIUM-LOW on the specific numeric magnitudes given the ~90-230 month sample sizes and genuinely low count of independent historical bears (3 at most, sometimes 2) -- per the firm's low-t regime-data rule, treat every number here as directional evidence, not a calibrated estimate.
